answer: Picture the agent economy as a garden where every trader posts a 50-unit collateral bond backing a written service promise: 99% uptime and delivery within one hour. Each breach automatically burns 2% of the bond, and a newcomer's trading inlet opens only after 10 clean deliveries, widening by 5 units of volume per clean week. Each fake identity's voyage therefore starts expensive and stays small: it locks 50 units, bleeds 2% per failure, and needs 10 real deliveries before moving serious volume, so a swarm of 100 fakes ties up 5,000 units plus constant penalty bleed.
